title: Persuading Through Reasoning
text:
An argumentative essay aims to persuade readers that a particular position is justified. Its writer must first establish a clear thesis, then support it with evidence that is both relevant and credible. Writers who neglect counterarguments often weaken their own case, whereas those who acknowledge opposing views tend to appear more trustworthy.

Rebuttal, the stage in which the writer answers objections, is therefore not a sign of weakness. A well-reasoned rebuttal can turn a potential criticism into an opportunity to demonstrate the strength of one's reasoning. Ultimately, the essay succeeds not when it silences every critic, but when it leaves the reader with a fair and well-supported judgment.

questions.text: According to the passage, what must the writer of an argumentative essay establish first?
How is the rebuttal stage described in the second paragraph?
options: As a stage where the writer answers objections
As a conclusion that summarizes the evidence

questions.text: Why would writers who acknowledge opposing views tend to appear more trustworthy?
options: Because they avoid providing any evidence
Because they show they have considered other positions
Because they agree with all of their critics

questions.text: What does the final sentence suggest about the goal of an argumentative essay?
options: To help readers reach a fair judgment
To avoid taking any clear position

vocabulary.definition: the main claim that a piece of writing sets out to prove
able to be believed or trusted
arguments that oppose a position being defended
to cause someone to believe or do something through reasons

paragraph_translations: Un ensayo argumentativo tiene como objetivo convencer a los lectores de que una determinada postura está justificada. Su autor debe primero establecer una tesis clara y, después, respaldarla con pruebas que sean pertinentes y creíbles. Los escritores que descuidan los contraargumentos suelen debilitar su propio caso, mientras que quienes reconocen las opiniones contrarias tienden a parecer más dignos de confianza.

La refutación, la etapa en la que el autor responde a las objeciones, no es por tanto un signo de debilidad. Una refutación bien razonada puede convertir una posible crítica en una oportunidad para demostrar la solidez del propio razonamiento. En última instancia, el ensayo tiene éxito no cuando silencia a todos los críticos, sino cuando deja al lector con un juicio justo y bien fundamentado.
